one_sentence: Title/authors/year/journal/volume/issue/pages all correctly identify Clarida-Galí-Gertler (2000, QJE 115(1):147-180) with no field-mixing, but the publisher is a JSTOR anachronism (Oxford University Press, which only took over QJE c. 2017-2018) and the entry lacks a DOI while carrying stray JSTOR-import fields (ISSN, abstract, urldate).

issues.reason: In 2000, The Quarterly Journal of Economics was published by MIT Press (MIT Press Journals operated the journal on behalf of copyright holder Harvard College); QJE only moved to Oxford University Press around 2017-2018 (starting near vol. 132). The 'Oxford University Press' value in this entry reflects JSTOR/Crossref's current-publisher-of-record metadata, not the publisher at the time of publication -- exactly the anachronism pattern flagged for JSTOR-sourced imports.

No DOI was present. 10.1162/003355300554692 resolves (via Crossref redirect) to the Oxford Academic landing page for this exact article (vol. 115, issue 1, pp. 147-180, 2000), confirming it as the canonical anchor.

Stray JSTOR-import field. ISSN values are correct (0033-5533 print / 1531-4650 online, matching JSTOR/ISSN portal records for QJE) but are non-standard clutter in a reference-list .bib entry once journal + volume + issue + DOI are present.
Stray JSTOR-import field; abstracts are not customary in a bibliography entry for a citation list and bloat the .bib without affecting the rendered reference.
Stray JSTOR-import field. urldate is meaningful for undated/online-only sources; this is a stable, DOI-identified print journal article, so an access date is superfluous.
